options.a: Diagnoses and symptoms/reasons for the encounter
options.b: Procedures and services performed by physicians
options.c: Supplies, drugs, and durable medical equipment
options.d: Inpatient hospital procedures and devices

distractorExplanations.b: Physician procedures and services are reported with CPT (HCPCS Level I), not with ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes.
distractorExplanations.c: Supplies, drugs and DME are reported with HCPCS Level II codes, not with ICD-10-CM.
distractorExplanations.d: Inpatient hospital procedures and devices are coded with ICD-10-PCS, the procedure system, not ICD-10-CM.

options.a: Emerging technologies tracked for data collection and assessment
options.b: Performance measures that support quality reporting programs
options.c: Established medical services and procedures widely performed
options.d: Supplies, drugs, and services not included in the CPT book

distractorExplanations.a: Emerging technologies tracked for data collection are CPT Category III codes (temporary, ending in T).
distractorExplanations.b: Performance measurement and quality reporting codes are CPT Category II codes (ending in F), not Category I.
distractorExplanations.d: Supplies, drugs and services outside CPT are reported with HCPCS Level II, a separate code set.

options.a: Not otherwise specified — the unspecified code
options.b: Newly established code — added this fiscal year
options.c: Non-essential condition — not required on claims
options.d: Not elsewhere classified — other specified

distractorExplanations.a: That is NOS: the documentation lacks detail, so the unspecified code is used; NEC means detail exists but no specific code.
distractorExplanations.b: New codes are identified in the annual code update tables; NEC is a residual-category convention, not a new-code flag.
distractorExplanations.c: NEC does not mark optional conditions; it directs the coder to the 'other specified' code when no precise code exists.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-coding-guidelin.explanation: NEC/NOS conventions guide residual code selection when documentation specificity is limited or classification lacks detail. NEC is used when the documented condition is specific but no more precise code is available.

options.a: A single code captures a condition and its manifestation
options.b: Two codes are needed to capture the etiology and its manifestation
options.c: A diagnosis is reported with a separate code for each symptom
options.d: One code is reported for multiple unrelated conditions seen that day

distractorExplanations.b: Two codes (etiology then manifestation) is the dual-coding convention used when no combination code exists.
distractorExplanations.c: Coding each symptom separately is the opposite of a combination code, which absorbs associated symptoms or complications.
distractorExplanations.d: Combination codes join related conditions or a condition with its complication, not unrelated conditions from one visit.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-coding-guidelin.explanation: Guidelines instruct use of combination codes when available rather than multiple codes unnecessarily. The combination code may also capture an associated condition or complication, as directed by the classification.

options.a: Advisory only, unlike the parenthetical notes beneath codes
options.b: Applicable to the first code listed under that heading
options.c: Instructional and must be followed for correct coding
options.d: Reference material for auditors, not for the coder assigning codes

distractorExplanations.a: Section guidelines are just as binding as parenthetical notes; both are instructional and govern code selection.
distractorExplanations.b: Section and heading guidelines apply to every code in that section or heading, not just the first code listed.
distractorExplanations.d: The guidelines direct the coder at the point of code assignment; they are not merely audit reference material.

options.a: Replace the injury code as the first-listed diagnosis
options.b: Report the nature of the injury, such as fracture or laceration
options.c: Identify the place of service where the injury was treated
options.d: Provide information about how an injury/poisoning occurred

distractorExplanations.a: External cause codes are never first-listed; they supplement the injury code, which stays sequenced first.
distractorExplanations.b: The nature of the injury (fracture, laceration) is coded in Chapter 19 S/T codes; external causes describe cause and intent.
distractorExplanations.c: Treatment setting is the claim POS field; Y92 place-of-occurrence codes describe where the injury happened.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-coding-guidelin.explanation: External causes supplement injury coding; they do not replace the injury diagnosis. Report them when required or assigned.

options.a: Left, right, or bilateral when the classification provides those options
options.b: Left or right only, with bilateral reported using two codes
options.c: The side most often affected by the condition when the note does not state one
options.d: Side information through modifiers RT/LT instead of the code

distractorExplanations.b: When a bilateral code exists it is used; separate left and right codes are only for conditions without a bilateral option.
distractorExplanations.c: If laterality is not documented the unspecified side code is assigned (or the provider queried); the side is never assumed.
distractorExplanations.d: RT/LT are HCPCS modifiers for procedure codes; ICD-10-CM laterality is built into the diagnosis code characters.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-coding-guidelin.explanation: Choose the most specific laterality code supported; unspecified if not documented. Laterality must also be supported by documentation.

options.a: Locate a candidate code in the Tabular List, then confirm it in the Alphabetic Index
options.b: Locate a candidate code in the Index, then verify and complete coding in the Tabular List
options.c: Assign the code shown in the Index when it is complete to all characters
options.d: Locate a code in the Index, then verify it against the payer's LCD list

distractorExplanations.a: The order is reversed: the Alphabetic Index is searched first, and the Tabular List is where the code is verified.
distractorExplanations.c: Even a code that looks complete in the Index must be verified in the Tabular for notes, excludes and 7th characters.
distractorExplanations.d: LCDs decide coverage, not code assignment; verification of the code itself happens in the Tabular List.

options.a: Code the suspected condition as if confirmed
options.b: Code signs, symptoms, or abnormal findings
options.c: Code a Z03 observation code for the possible condition
options.d: Code R69 illness unspecified until tests return

distractorExplanations.a: Coding uncertain diagnoses as confirmed is the inpatient rule; outpatient coding goes to the highest degree of certainty.
distractorExplanations.c: Z03 observation codes apply when a suspected condition is ruled out and no signs or symptoms are present.
distractorExplanations.d: R69 is a nonspecific code; documented signs and symptoms are more specific and are coded instead.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-coding-guidelin.explanation: Outpatient guidelines allow coding of documented signs/symptoms when no confirmed diagnosis exists. Code those documented as the reason for the encounter.

options.a: ICD-10-PCS (inpatient)
options.b: CPT (HCPCS Level I)
options.c: HCPCS Level II
options.d: ICD-10-CM (diagnoses)

distractorExplanations.a: ICD-10-PCS reports inpatient facility procedures on hospital claims, not physician services on professional claims.
distractorExplanations.c: HCPCS Level II mainly reports supplies, drugs, DME and some services not in CPT, not core physician procedures.
distractorExplanations.d: ICD-10-CM reports diagnoses and reasons for the encounter; procedures and services are reported with CPT.

options.a: The excluded condition may be coded additionally when it is present
options.b: The conditions are mutually exclusive and should not be coded together
options.c: The excluded condition must be sequenced first when both are present
options.d: The code requires an additional code to identify the manifestation present

distractorExplanations.a: 'May be coded additionally when present' describes Excludes2 (not included here), not the pure Excludes1 exclusion.
distractorExplanations.c: Sequencing directions come from 'code first' notes; Excludes1 says the two codes are not reported together.
distractorExplanations.d: Requiring a manifestation code is a 'use additional code' instruction, unrelated to an Excludes1 note.

options.a: Inpatient facility procedures reported on the hospital UB-04 claim
options.b: Supplies, drugs, durable medical equipment, and certain services not in CPT
options.c: Emerging technology services tracked with temporary Category III codes
options.d: Physician office visits, surgeries, and diagnostic tests

distractorExplanations.a: Inpatient facility procedures on the UB-04 are coded with ICD-10-PCS, not HCPCS Level II.
distractorExplanations.c: Category III codes for emerging technology are part of CPT (HCPCS Level I), not HCPCS Level II.
distractorExplanations.d: Office visits, surgeries and diagnostic tests are CPT (HCPCS Level I) codes, not Level II.

options.a: The patient's home address region for payment locality
options.b: The setting where the service was rendered
options.c: The type of provider, such as a physician or nurse practitioner
options.d: The facility's NPI and billing address

distractorExplanations.a: POS is not the patient's address; payment locality follows where the service was furnished, not where the patient lives.
distractorExplanations.c: Provider type and specialty are shown by the taxonomy code, not the two-digit place-of-service code.
distractorExplanations.d: Facility NPI and address go in the service facility and billing provider fields (boxes 32-33), not the POS code.

options.a: Medical decision making or total time on the date of the encounter
options.b: History, exam, and MDM, with all three key components required
options.c: Face-to-face time, when counseling exceeds 50 percent of the visit
options.d: Number of exam bullets documented under the 1997 guidelines

distractorExplanations.b: The three-key-component model was retired for office/outpatient E/M in 2021; history and exam are now only 'medically appropriate'.
distractorExplanations.c: The 50 percent counseling rule is the pre-2021 time rule; current office E/M uses total time on the date, including non-face-to-face.
distractorExplanations.d: Counting 1997 exam bullets no longer selects office E/M levels; the exam does not drive the level at all since 2021.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-evaluation-mana.explanation: Since 2021 office E/M revisions, MDM or time drives levels; older exam-bullet counting is not the current office paradigm. Apply the CPT guidelines for whichever basis is used.

options.a: The past two years
options.b: The past three years
options.c: The past five years
options.d: The past seven years

distractorExplanations.a: Two years is too short; CPT treats a patient as established if seen by the same specialty/group within the past three years.
distractorExplanations.c: Five years is not the CPT rule; after three years without a face-to-face service the patient is new again.
distractorExplanations.d: Seven years is a common records-retention figure, not the CPT new-versus-established patient window of three years.

options.a: History, examination, and the number of diagnoses documented
options.b: Problems addressed, total time spent, and number of orders placed
options.c: Number/complexity of problems, data reviewed/analyzed, and risk
options.d: Number of problems, the exam level, and risk of complications

distractorExplanations.a: History and exam are not MDM elements; MDM is problems, data reviewed/analyzed, and risk of patient management.
distractorExplanations.b: Total time is an alternative basis for leveling, not an element of MDM; orders count only within the data element.
distractorExplanations.d: The exam level is not part of MDM, and this omits the data reviewed/analyzed element.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-evaluation-mana.explanation: MDM elements are problems, data, and risk under AMA E/M methodology. Risk refers to the risk of patient management.

options.a: Face-to-face time only, counted from when the provider enters the room
options.b: Time spent by clinical staff rooming the patient and taking vitals
options.c: Provider time on the patient's care across the entire week of the visit
options.d: Total time on the date of the encounter spent on the patient's care

distractorExplanations.a: Since 2021 office E/M time is total provider time on the date, including non-face-to-face work, not just room time.
distractorExplanations.b: Clinical staff time is excluded; only physician or other qualified health professional time counts toward the level.
distractorExplanations.c: Only time on the date of the encounter counts; work on other days of the week is not added to the visit.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-evaluation-mana.explanation: Counseling/coordination and other activities on that date may count when using time, per definitions. This includes non-face-to-face activities on that date, per CPT rules.

options.a: Focuses on routine preventive evaluation appropriate to age/risk
options.b: Is selected by MDM level, the same way as other office E/M visits
options.c: Requires a chief complaint to support medical necessity
options.d: Is coded by total time spent on the date of service

distractorExplanations.b: Preventive medicine codes are chosen by new versus established status and patient age, not by MDM level.
distractorExplanations.c: Preventive visits are not complaint-driven; they are reported with Z00-type encounter codes rather than a problem.
distractorExplanations.d: Preventive medicine codes are not time-based; time leveling applies to problem-oriented office E/M codes.

options.a: Decision for surgery made at an E/M visit the day before a major procedure
options.b: Significant, separately identifiable E/M service on the same day as a procedure
options.c: Unrelated E/M service by the same physician during a postoperative period
options.d: Distinct procedural service that is normally bundled with another procedure

distractorExplanations.a: A decision for major surgery at the visit the day before or day of surgery is reported with modifier 57, not 25.
distractorExplanations.c: An unrelated E/M during the postoperative period by the same physician is reported with modifier 24.
distractorExplanations.d: Distinct procedural services that are normally bundled use modifier 59 or the X{EPSU} modifiers, not 25.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-evaluation-mana.explanation: Modifier 25 appends to the E/M, not the procedure, when documentation supports separateness. It is reported by the same physician on the E/M code.

options.a: At least 15 minutes of care for a patient in an intensive care unit
options.b: Moderate-complexity decision making for any patient seen in the ED
options.c: High-complexity decision making for critically ill/injured patients
options.d: High-complexity decision making for a stable patient in an ICU bed

distractorExplanations.a: Location does not define critical care, and 99291 needs at least 30 minutes of critical care time, not 15.
distractorExplanations.b: Moderate MDM in the ED is an ED E/M service; critical care needs high-complexity care of a critically ill patient.
distractorExplanations.d: A stable patient in an ICU bed is coded with hospital care codes; the ICU location alone is not critical care.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-evaluation-mana.explanation: Critical care is a defined CPT service with time and clinical criteria—not ordinary E/M. Specific time thresholds apply (99291 covers the first 30-74 minutes).

options.a: Assuming ongoing management of the patient at another provider's request
options.b: Advice/opinion offered when the patient self-refers to a specialist
options.c: A request from another provider with no written report required
options.d: Advice/opinion requested by another provider, with report back

distractorExplanations.a: Taking over ongoing management is a transfer of care, which is reported with regular E/M codes, not a consultation.
distractorExplanations.b: A patient-initiated specialist visit is not a consultation; the request must come from a physician or other provider.
distractorExplanations.c: A consultation requires a written report back to the requesting provider; omitting it fails the request-render-report test.

options.a: Where the service was rendered
options.b: The billing provider's office address
options.c: Where the patient lives for locality pricing
options.d: The type of provider who rendered the service

distractorExplanations.b: The billing address goes in box 33; the POS code describes the setting where the service took place.
distractorExplanations.c: Locality pricing follows where the service was furnished; the patient's residence is not what POS reports.
distractorExplanations.d: Provider type and specialty are shown by the taxonomy code, not by the two-digit place-of-service code.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-evaluation-mana.explanation: POS affects payment and must match the service setting. Examples include office, outpatient hospital, and ED.

options.a: A patient's own request for a specialist opinion and a written report
options.b: A request for opinion/advice, rendering of services, and a written report
options.c: A request for opinion/advice and the consultant assuming ongoing care
options.d: A provider's request for advice, with a verbal update instead of a report

distractorExplanations.a: A patient-initiated request does not qualify; consultations require a request from a physician or other appropriate source.
distractorExplanations.c: Assuming ongoing care is a transfer of care, which is not reported with consultation codes.
distractorExplanations.d: The consultant must send a written report back; a verbal update alone fails the report requirement.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-evaluation-mana.explanation: Classic consult requirements: request, render, report (payer policies vary) The report goes back to the requesting source.

options.a: Total time the ED physician spent on the date of the encounter
options.b: The documented key components/MDM appropriate to ED E/M levels
options.c: The triage acuity level assigned by the ED nurse at arrival
options.d: The number of diagnostic tests ordered during the ED visit

distractorExplanations.a: ED E/M codes are not selected by time because ED care is shift-based; the office total-time rule does not apply.
distractorExplanations.c: Nursing triage acuity (such as ESI) is a facility measure, not the basis for the physician's ED E/M level.
distractorExplanations.d: Tests ordered feed only the data element of MDM; they do not alone determine the ED E/M level.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-evaluation-mana.explanation: ED E/M leveling follows ED-specific CPT rules emphasizing history/exam/MDM as applicable. Office time rules do not apply to ED levels.

options.a: Reporting both services, with modifier 25 on the preventive E/M
options.b: Reporting both services, with modifier 25 on the problem E/M
options.c: Reporting only the preventive code and adding the problem's diagnosis
options.d: Reporting both services, with modifier 59 on the problem E/M

distractorExplanations.a: Modifier 25 goes on the problem-oriented office E/M code, not on the preventive medicine code.
distractorExplanations.c: When the problem work is significant and separately identifiable, the problem E/M is also reportable, not just a diagnosis.
distractorExplanations.d: Modifier 59 is for distinct procedures, not E/M services; a separate E/M on the same day uses modifier 25.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-evaluation-mana.explanation: Significant separately identifiable problem E/M may be reported with preventive care using modifier 25. Both are reported when the problem is significant and separately identifiable.

options.a: Local infiltration, certain related E/M, and routine postoperative care
options.b: Treatment of postoperative complications that require a return to the OR
options.c: General anesthesia provided by a separate anesthesia professional
options.d: Unrelated E/M visits by the surgeon during the postoperative period

distractorExplanations.b: A return to the OR for complications is separately reportable with modifier 78; it is not part of the package.
distractorExplanations.c: Anesthesia by a separate anesthesia provider is billed separately; only local, metacarpal/digital block or topical is included.
distractorExplanations.d: Unrelated E/M visits during the global period are separately reportable with modifier 24.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-surgery-anesthe.explanation: CPT surgical package and payer global periods define what is bundled vs separately reportable. Coverage applies within the global period as defined.

options.a: Staged or planned related procedure by the same physician during the postoperative period
options.b: Unplanned return to the OR for a related procedure during the postoperative period
options.c: Unrelated procedure by the same physician during the postoperative period
options.d: Repeat procedure by the same physician after the original procedure

distractorExplanations.a: A staged, planned or more extensive related procedure in the global period is modifier 58, not the unplanned 78.
distractorExplanations.c: An unrelated procedure by the same physician during the postoperative period is reported with modifier 79.
distractorExplanations.d: A repeat procedure by the same physician is modifier 76; 78 is an unplanned return to the OR for a related procedure.

options.a: Determine whether a service is medically necessary for the diagnosis coded
options.b: Assign the relative value units used to price each CPT code
options.c: Prevent improper reporting of services that should not be billed together
options.d: Identify procedures that require prior authorization by Medicare

distractorExplanations.a: Medical necessity for a diagnosis is set by NCDs and LCDs, not by NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits.
distractorExplanations.b: RVUs come from the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (RBRVS), not from NCCI edits.
distractorExplanations.d: Prior authorization lists are separate Medicare programs; NCCI edits address code pairs and units, not PA.

options.a: CPT surgical codes with modifier 47 and anesthesia time in minutes
options.b: CPT anesthesia codes with base units plus RVUs taken from the surgery code
options.c: ICD-10-PCS anesthesia section codes on the professional claim
options.d: CPT anesthesia codes with base units + time units + modifying units

distractorExplanations.a: Modifier 47 is for anesthesia by the surgeon; anesthesia providers report CPT anesthesia codes 00100-01999 with time.
distractorExplanations.b: Anesthesia payment uses base units plus time units times the anesthesia conversion factor, not surgical RVUs.
distractorExplanations.c: ICD-10-PCS is for inpatient facility procedures and has no professional anesthesia codes; professionals use CPT.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-surgery-anesthe.explanation: Anesthesia payment formulas combine base and time; physical status/qualifying circumstances may apply. Payer rules govern the modifying units.

options.a: Multiple procedures performed at the same session by the same provider
options.b: Bilateral procedures performed at the same session by the same provider
options.c: A distinct procedure performed at a separate session on the same day
options.d: Two surgeons performing distinct parts of the same procedure

distractorExplanations.b: Bilateral procedures at the same session are reported with modifier 50, not modifier 51.
distractorExplanations.c: A distinct procedure at a separate session is reported with modifier 59 or XE, not modifier 51.
distractorExplanations.d: Two surgeons performing distinct parts of one procedure is co-surgery, reported with modifier 62.

options.a: The code is reported with modifier 51 whenever it is billed
options.b: The code is not reported in addition when integral
options.c: The code may be billed only when performed on a separate day
options.d: The code is an add-on reported in addition to the larger service

distractorExplanations.a: Modifier 51 marks multiple procedures; the separate procedure designation does not require modifier 51.
distractorExplanations.c: A separate procedure can be reported on the same day when done alone or at a distinct site/session (with 59/X modifiers).
distractorExplanations.d: Add-on codes are marked with '+'; separate procedures are bundled when integral, not added on.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-surgery-anesthe.explanation: If performed alone for a distinct reason, a 'separate procedure' may be reportable; otherwise bundled. The code is usually a component of a larger service.

options.a: Complexity, number of sutures placed, and the patient's age
options.b: Length of each wound reported separately, with location ignored
options.c: Complexity (simple/intermediate/complex), length, and location
options.d: Wound depth, anesthetic used, and time spent on the repair

distractorExplanations.a: Suture count and patient age are not CPT repair criteria; complexity, summed length and anatomic location are.
distractorExplanations.b: Lengths of same-complexity repairs in the same anatomic grouping are summed, and location changes the code range.
distractorExplanations.d: Local anesthesia is included and time is not a criterion; depth matters only through the complexity classification.

options.a: 0-day, 30-day, and 60-day globals depending on the procedure
options.b: 10-day globals for minor and 30-day globals for major procedures
options.c: 90-day globals for every surgery, counted from the date of admission
options.d: 0-day, 10-day, and 90-day globals depending on the procedure

distractorExplanations.a: Medicare global periods are 0, 10 and 90 days; 30-day and 60-day globals are not Medicare global indicators.
distractorExplanations.b: Major procedures carry a 90-day global (plus the day before surgery), not 30 days.
distractorExplanations.c: Minor procedures have 0- or 10-day globals, and the 90-day period runs from the day after surgery, not admission.

options.a: Another surgeon assists the primary surgeon
options.b: Two surgeons perform distinct parts of one procedure
options.c: A nonphysician practitioner assists at surgery
options.d: A team of surgeons performs a complex procedure together

distractorExplanations.b: Two surgeons performing distinct parts of one procedure is co-surgery, reported with modifier 62.
distractorExplanations.c: PA, NP or CNS assistants at surgery are reported with modifier AS for Medicare, not modifier 80.
distractorExplanations.d: Team surgery for a complex procedure is reported with modifier 66, not an assistant surgeon modifier.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-surgery-anesthe.explanation: Documentation must support necessity; payer assistant policies vary (including PA/NP assisting modifiers). Assistance must be medically necessary and allowed by the payer.

options.a: A bullet (●) symbol and are reported after the primary procedure
options.b: A '+' symbol and are never reported as stand-alone primary codes
options.c: A lightning bolt and are reported with modifier 51 attached
options.d: A null symbol (⊘) and are exempt from multiple procedure rules

distractorExplanations.a: The bullet (●) marks new codes in the current CPT edition; add-on codes are marked with a plus sign.
distractorExplanations.c: The lightning bolt marks vaccine codes pending FDA approval, and add-on codes are exempt from modifier 51.
distractorExplanations.d: The null symbol (⊘) marks modifier 51 exempt codes, which are primary codes, not add-on codes.

options.a: The procedure plus any E/M visit during the global period, related or not
options.b: The procedure and related typical pre-/intra-/postoperative care
options.c: The procedure plus anesthesia provided by a separate anesthesiologist
options.d: The procedure only, with each postoperative visit billed separately

distractorExplanations.a: Unrelated E/M visits in the global period are separately reportable with modifier 24; only related care is bundled.
distractorExplanations.c: Anesthesia by a separate anesthesiologist is billed by that provider; only local or topical anesthesia is in the package.
distractorExplanations.d: Routine related postoperative visits are included in the package and are not billed separately.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-surgery-anesthe.explanation: Global surgical package covers the operation and routine related care in the global period. The package covers this care for the global period.

options.a: Bilateral procedures performed at the same session by the same provider
options.b: Multiple procedures performed at the same session by the same provider
options.c: Two surgeons performing distinct parts of one procedure
options.d: A procedure discontinued after anesthesia was administered

distractorExplanations.a: Bilateral procedures at the same session are reported with modifier 50, not modifier 51.
distractorExplanations.c: Two surgeons performing distinct parts of one procedure is co-surgery, reported with modifier 62.
distractorExplanations.d: A discontinued procedure is reported by the physician with modifier 53, not the multiple-procedure modifier 51.

options.a: The surgeon makes the first incision after induction is complete
options.b: The anesthesiologist begins to prepare the patient for anesthesia
options.c: The anesthesiologist completes the preoperative assessment in holding
options.d: The patient is intubated and induction is complete

distractorExplanations.a: Incision comes well after anesthesia time starts; time begins when the anesthesiologist starts preparing the patient.
distractorExplanations.c: The preanesthesia evaluation is included in the base units, so it is not counted as anesthesia time.
distractorExplanations.d: Time starts with preparation for induction, before intubation, not after induction is complete.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-surgery-anesthe.explanation: Anesthesia time starts with preparation for anesthesia induction and ends when the anesthesiologist is no longer in personal attendance. Preparation takes place in the OR or procedure area.

options.a: Reported in addition to a larger related procedure, with modifier 51 appended
options.b: Usually considered integral to a larger procedure and not separately reported
options.c: Reportable only with modifier 59 even when performed alone
options.d: An add-on code reported with the primary procedure it supports

distractorExplanations.a: When integral to the larger related procedure it is bundled; modifier 51 does not make it separately payable.
distractorExplanations.c: When performed alone it is reported without any modifier; 59/X modifiers apply only with another procedure.
distractorExplanations.d: Add-on codes carry a '+' and are always secondary; separate procedures are standalone codes bundled when integral.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-surgery-anesthe.explanation: “Separate procedure” codes are typically not unbundled from a more comprehensive related procedure. This applies when it is performed as part of that larger service.

options.a: The patient's ASA physical status classification
options.b: The anesthesia provider's level of medical direction
options.c: Qualifying circumstances such as extreme age or emergency
options.d: The base unit value assigned to the anesthesia code

distractorExplanations.b: Medical direction or supervision level is shown with modifiers AA, QK, QX, QY and QZ, not P1-P6.
distractorExplanations.c: Extreme age, emergency and similar factors are reported with qualifying circumstance codes 99100-99140.
distractorExplanations.d: Base units come from the anesthesia code itself; P modifiers report the patient's ASA physical status.

options.a: Reporting a higher-level service than documented/supported
options.b: Reporting a lower level than documented to avoid payer audits
options.c: Billing component codes separately instead of one bundled code
options.d: Billing for a service that the provider did not perform

distractorExplanations.b: Reporting a lower level than documented is downcoding (undercoding), also noncompliant but the opposite of upcoding.
distractorExplanations.c: Billing components instead of the bundled code is unbundling, a different improper coding practice.
distractorExplanations.d: Billing for services not rendered is phantom billing, a separate fraud type from inflating a real service's level.

options.a: Honest clerical corrections via timely voids/replacements
options.b: Knowingly submitting false or fraudulent claims to the government
options.c: Accepting gifts from vendors in exchange for patient referrals
options.d: Physician referrals to a lab the physician has a financial interest in

distractorExplanations.c: Paying or accepting remuneration for referrals is addressed by the Anti-Kickback Statute, not the False Claims Act itself.
distractorExplanations.d: Self-referral to an entity with a financial relationship is governed by the Stark Law, not the False Claims Act itself.
distractorExplanations.a: Good-faith corrections differ.

options.a: Workplace safety rules and sharps injury logs
options.b: Electronic transaction formats and code set standards
options.c: Protected health information use and disclosure
options.d: Technical safeguards such as encryption and access logs

distractorExplanations.a: Workplace safety and sharps injury logs are OSHA requirements, not part of the HIPAA Privacy Rule.
distractorExplanations.b: Transaction formats and code sets fall under the HIPAA Transactions and Code Sets rule, not the Privacy Rule.
distractorExplanations.d: Technical safeguards for electronic PHI are required by the HIPAA Security Rule, separate from the Privacy Rule.

options.a: Diagnoses, symptoms, and reasons for the patient encounter
options.b: Inpatient facility procedures on the UB-04
options.c: Emerging technology services tracked with Category III codes
options.d: Drugs, supplies, DME, and certain services not in CPT

distractorExplanations.a: Diagnoses, symptoms and encounter reasons are reported with ICD-10-CM, not HCPCS Level II.
distractorExplanations.b: Inpatient facility procedures on the UB-04 are coded with ICD-10-PCS, not HCPCS Level II.
distractorExplanations.c: Category III codes for emerging technology belong to CPT (HCPCS Level I), not HCPCS Level II.

options.a: A provider believes Medicare may deny a service as not reasonable/necessary
options.b: A Medicare Advantage enrollee may owe for a service the plan will not cover
options.c: A hospital inpatient is told about the right to appeal a discharge decision
options.d: A patient is notified that Medicaid will be billed as the secondary payer

distractorExplanations.b: The ABN is not used for Medicare Advantage enrollees; MA plans handle this through organization determinations.
distractorExplanations.c: Inpatient discharge appeal rights are given on the Important Message from Medicare (IM), not the ABN.
distractorExplanations.d: Secondary-payer billing is coordination of benefits; the ABN addresses expected Medicare denial and patient liability.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-compliance-bill.explanation: ABN shifts financial liability for expected denials when properly executed for Medicare Part B situations. The beneficiary may then be financially liable.

options.a: A patient's unique Medicare Beneficiary Identifier shown on claims
options.b: A unique identification number for covered health care providers
options.c: A taxonomy code describing the provider's type and specialty
options.d: A federal tax ID used to report the practice's income

distractorExplanations.a: The Medicare Beneficiary Identifier identifies the patient; the NPI identifies the health care provider.
distractorExplanations.c: The taxonomy code is a separate 10-character code describing provider type and specialty, not the NPI itself.
distractorExplanations.d: The federal tax ID (EIN/TIN) is used for tax reporting; the NPI is a 10-digit provider identifier for HIPAA transactions.

options.a: Reporting a higher E/M level than the documentation supports
options.b: Reporting the comprehensive panel code when all component tests were done
options.c: Billing component codes separately when a comprehensive code includes them
options.d: Appending modifier 59 when services are distinct and documented

distractorExplanations.a: Reporting a higher level than documented is upcoding, a different compliance violation from unbundling.
distractorExplanations.b: Using the panel code when every component test was performed is correct coding, the opposite of unbundling.
distractorExplanations.d: Modifier 59 on truly distinct, documented services is appropriate use, not unbundling.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-compliance-bill.explanation: Unbundling to increase payment violates NCCI/CPT inclusive coding principles. Billing the components this way is contrary to CPT and NCCI rules.

options.a: Services the patient requests and agrees to pay for out of pocket
options.b: Services that are covered benefits under the patient's plan
options.c: Services ordered by a physician, which makes them necessary
options.d: Services are reasonable and necessary for diagnosis/treatment

distractorExplanations.a: Patient willingness to pay does not establish medical necessity; the clinical need must be documented.
distractorExplanations.b: Being a covered benefit is a coverage question; a covered service can still be denied as not medically necessary.
distractorExplanations.c: A physician order alone does not make a service necessary; the documentation must support the clinical need.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-compliance-bill.explanation: Coverage policies/LCDs/NCDs define necessity; documentation must support it. Necessity is judged against payer coverage criteria.

options.a: Policies, training, auditing, and a process to report/respond to issues
options.b: Policies and training, with audits done only after a payer complaint
options.c: Policies, training, and audits, with no anonymous reporting line
options.d: Auditing and training, with discipline left out of written standards

distractorExplanations.b: OIG guidance calls for ongoing internal auditing and monitoring, not audits triggered after a payer complaint.
distractorExplanations.c: Open lines of communication, including an anonymous reporting option, are one of the OIG's seven core elements.
distractorExplanations.d: Enforcing standards through well-publicized disciplinary guidelines is one of the OIG's seven core elements.

options.a: A significant, separately identifiable E/M service on the day of a procedure
options.b: A distinct procedural service not normally reported together
options.c: A bilateral procedure performed at the same operative session
options.d: A repeat procedure by the same physician on the same day

distractorExplanations.a: A significant, separately identifiable E/M on the day of a procedure is reported with modifier 25, not 59.
distractorExplanations.c: Bilateral procedures at the same session are reported with modifier 50, not 59 or the X modifiers.
distractorExplanations.d: A repeat procedure by the same physician is reported with modifier 76, not the distinct-service modifier 59.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-compliance-bill.explanation: Use distinct-service modifiers only with documentation; overuse is an audit target. Use it only when the criteria are met.

options.a: Billing errors made in good faith and refunded within 60 days
options.b: Knowingly submitting false or fraudulent claims for government payment
options.c: Kickbacks paid to induce referrals of federal health program patients
options.d: Disclosure of patient information without authorization

distractorExplanations.a: Good-faith errors refunded promptly lack the knowing intent the False Claims Act requires for liability.
distractorExplanations.c: Kickbacks for referrals are addressed by the Anti-Kickback Statute, a separate law from the False Claims Act.
distractorExplanations.d: Unauthorized disclosure of PHI is a HIPAA Privacy Rule violation, not a False Claims Act matter.

options.a: Reporting a lower-level service than documented to limit audit risk
options.b: Reporting a higher-level service than supported by documentation
options.c: Billing separately for components included in a comprehensive code
options.d: Billing a service that was not performed, using a valid code

distractorExplanations.a: Reporting a lower level than documented is downcoding, which is also inaccurate but the opposite of upcoding.
distractorExplanations.c: Billing components of a comprehensive code separately is unbundling, a distinct improper coding practice.
distractorExplanations.d: Billing for a service not performed is billing for services not rendered, a separate fraud type from upcoding.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-compliance-bill.explanation: Upcoding is a compliance risk and potential fraud when unsupported. It is typically done to increase payment.

options.a: Set coverage rules that define medical necessity for each service
options.b: Prevent improper payment of services that should not be billed together
options.c: Assign relative value units used to price each CPT code
options.d: Identify the global surgical period assigned to each procedure code

distractorExplanations.a: Coverage and medical necessity rules come from NCDs and LCDs, not from NCCI edits.
distractorExplanations.c: Relative value units come from the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (RBRVS), not from NCCI edits.
distractorExplanations.d: Global surgical days are indicators in the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule database, not NCCI edits.

options.a: Notify a beneficiary that Medicaid will cover the balance
options.b: Notify a beneficiary that Medicare may deny a service
options.c: Notify an inpatient of the right to appeal a hospital discharge
options.d: Document the patient's consent to the procedure being performed

distractorExplanations.a: The ABN shifts potential liability to the beneficiary; it does not promise Medicaid will pay the balance.
distractorExplanations.c: Inpatient discharge appeal rights are given on the Important Message from Medicare (IM), not the ABN.
distractorExplanations.d: The ABN is a financial liability notice; consent to the procedure is a separate clinical document.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-compliance-bill.explanation: ABNs shift potential financial liability for anticipated Medicare noncoverage when properly used. This lets the beneficiary decide whether to accept financial responsibility.

options.a: The service is a covered benefit under the patient's plan
options.b: The service is reasonable and necessary for diagnosis or treatment
options.c: The service was ordered by a licensed physician for the patient
options.d: The service is requested by the patient after informed consent

distractorExplanations.a: Being a covered benefit is a coverage question; a covered service can still be denied as not medically necessary.
distractorExplanations.c: A physician order alone does not establish necessity; documentation must show the clinical need for the service.
distractorExplanations.d: A patient request, even with informed consent, does not make a service medically necessary.

aapc-cpc-readiness-check-compliance-bill.explanation: Coverage depends on documented medical necessity aligned with payer policies. It must meet payer/coverage rules and be supported by documentation.
